questions.title: What exactly makes GRPO "ill-posed"—bias, variance, or unit mismatch?
questions.question_body: The paper says GRPO is ill-posed because it applies token-level importance weights $w_{i,t} = \frac{\pi_\theta(y_{i,t}\mid x,y_{i,<t})}{\pi_{\theta_\text{old}}(y_{i,t}\mid x,y_{i,<t})}$ while rewards are given at the sequence level. Can you make precise what "ill-posed" means here? Is the gradient estimator biased, does its variance explode with sequence length $|y|$, or is it a mismatch between the unit of reward (sequence) and the unit of optimization (token) that breaks an assumption? A small counterexample or formal statement would help.

questions.title: Deriving GSPO from importance sampling: what target expectation is being estimated?
questions.question_body: GSPO optimizes $\mathbb{E}_{y \sim \pi_{\theta_\text{old}}(\cdot \mid x)}[\min(s_i(\theta)\hat A_i, \operatorname{clip}(s_i(\theta),1-\varepsilon,1+\varepsilon)\hat A_i)]$ with $s_i(\theta) = \left(\frac{\pi_\theta(y_i\mid x)}{\pi_{\theta_\text{old}}(y_i\mid x)}\right)^{1/|y_i|}$. If we start from the desired on-policy objective $\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\mathcal D, y\sim\pi_\theta(\cdot\mid x)}[A(x,y)]$ (with groupwise normalized advantages), what exact importance-sampling steps lead to the unclipped GSPO surrogate $\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi_{\theta_\text{old}}}[s_i(\theta) A(x,y)]$? Is the $1/|y|$ exponent merely a variance-reduction heuristic or part of a principled derivation?

questions.title: Why raise the sequence importance ratio to the power $1/|y|$ (geometric mean of token ratios)?
questions.question_body: GSPO defines $s_i(\theta) = \left(\frac{\pi_\theta(y_i\mid x)}{\pi_{\theta_\text{old}}(y_i\mid x)}\right)^{1/|y_i|} = \exp\left(\tfrac{1}{|y_i|}\sum_t \log\tfrac{\pi_\theta(y_{i,t}\mid x,y_{i,<t})}{\pi_{\theta_\text{old}}(y_{i,t}\mid x,y_{i,<t})}\right)$. I see that this is the geometric mean of per-token ratios. Does using the geometric mean change the fixed point compared to using the raw ratio $\frac{\pi_\theta(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\theta_\text{old}}(y\mid x)}$? Can you quantify how this normalization affects bias/variance and why it improves numerical stability without altering the optimization target?

questions.title: Does the $1/|y|$ factor in the GSPO gradient introduce a length bias?
questions.question_body: The GSPO gradient is proportional to $\frac{1}{|y|}\sum_t \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(y_t\mid x,y_{<t})$, i.e., an average rather than a sum. Does this averaging reduce the learning signal for longer sequences and subtly favor shorter responses? How does this interact with rewards that naturally increase with reasoning depth, and what happens if we remove or change the $1/|y|$ factor?

questions.title: How should we select the clipping range $\varepsilon$ in GSPO and why is it so small (e.g., $3\mathrm{e}{-4}$ to $4\mathrm{e}{-4}$)?
questions.question_body: In the experiments, GSPO uses left/right clipping ranges around $3\times10^{-4}$ to $4\times10^{-4}$, while GRPO uses values like $0.2$ and $0.27$. Given $s_i(\theta)$ is a geometric mean of token ratios (thus closer to 1), how should we calibrate $\varepsilon$ as a function of sequence length and expected policy shift per update? Is there a rule of thumb tying $\varepsilon$ to a target per-token KL or to $\mathbb{E}[\log s_i]$?

questions.title: Why define $s_{i,t}(\theta)$ with a stop-gradient trick in GSPO-token instead of using $s_i$ directly?
questions.question_body: GSPO-token sets $s_{i,t}(\theta) = \operatorname{sg}[s_i(\theta)] \cdot \frac{\pi_\theta(y_{i,t}\mid x,y_{i,<t})}{\operatorname{sg}[\pi_\theta(y_{i,t}\mid x,y_{i,<t})]}$, which is numerically equal to $s_i(\theta)$, but yields a gradient proportional to $s_i(\theta)\,\nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(y_{i,t}\mid x,y_{i,<t})$. Could you show the autograd steps that motivate this construction, and explain why simply multiplying $s_i(\theta)$ by per-token advantages would not produce the desired token-level gradient?

questions.title: Is GSPO unbiased in the on-policy limit, and what are the biases from clipping and groupwise normalization?
questions.question_body: If $\pi_\theta = \pi_{\theta_\text{old}}$ (on-policy), is the GSPO estimator $\mathbb{E}[s_i(\theta)\hat A_i]$ an unbiased estimator of the policy gradient with a baseline? How do clipping and groupwise $z$-score normalization (subtracting the group mean and dividing by the group std) introduce bias, and under what conditions does that bias vanish?

questions.title: Why is a single per-token importance weight considered "invalid" here while PPO commonly uses it?
questions.question_body: The paper argues that using $\frac{\pi_\theta(y_t\mid x,y_{<t})}{\pi_{\theta_\text{old}}(y_t\mid x,y_{<t})}$ at each step is a misapplication of importance sampling because it is based on one sample per next-token distribution and accumulates high variance. But standard PPO in control problems also uses a single action sample per state. What is different in sequence modeling that makes the variance accumulation problematic here? Is the mismatch primarily due to assigning a sequence-level advantage to each token (unit mismatch), sequence length compounding variance, or MoE routing volatility?

questions.title: Can you quantify the variance reduction from token-wise ratios to sequence-wise ratios?
questions.question_body: Is there an analysis comparing $\operatorname{Var}\left[\sum_t w_t \nabla\log\pi(y_t\mid\cdot)\right]$ versus $\operatorname{Var}\left[s\,\tfrac{1}{|y|}\sum_t \nabla\log\pi(y_t\mid\cdot)\right]$, where $w_t$ are per-token ratios and $s$ is the sequence-level geometric-mean ratio? Any bounds or empirical measurements showing how variance scales with $|y|$ in GRPO vs GSPO would clarify the claimed stabilization.

questions.title: What keeps the sequence-level ratio $s_i(\theta)$ from becoming extreme on long sequences?
questions.question_body: Even with the $1/|y|$ exponent, if a few tokens have large log-ratio deviations, could $s_i(\theta) = \exp\left(\tfrac{1}{|y|}\sum_t \log\tfrac{\pi_\theta}{\pi_{\theta_\text{old}}}\right)$ still become very small or large? How do length normalization and sequence-level clipping interact to bound the effective weight, and is there a recommended maximum sequence length or per-update KL target to keep $s_i$ in a safe range?

questions.title: What exact objective does GSPO's clipped surrogate lower-bound or approximate?
questions.question_body: PPO’s clipped surrogate is often motivated as a lower bound on a KL-constrained improvement. Does GSPO’s sequence-level clipping yield a similar monotonic improvement guarantee or a lower bound on an objective like $\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi_\theta}[A(x,y)]$ under a trust-region constraint on $\pi_\theta(\cdot\mid x)$ at the sequence level? If so, could you outline the bound and assumptions; if not, how should we interpret the surrogate theoretically?

questions.title: How does groupwise $z$-scoring of rewards interact with off-policy correction?
questions.question_body: Each response’s advantage is $\hat A_i = \frac{r(x,y_i) - \operatorname{mean}(\{r\})}{\operatorname{std}(\{r\})}$ computed within the group sampled from $\pi_{\theta_\text{old}}$. Since this baseline and scale depend on the sampled group, does this introduce bias in the off-policy estimator with importance weights $s_i(\theta)$? Are there conditions (e.g., large group size $G$) under which the bias becomes negligible?

questions.title: Why can clipping a larger fraction of tokens still yield higher training efficiency in GSPO?
questions.question_body: The paper reports that GSPO clips many more tokens (because entire responses are clipped) yet achieves better sample efficiency than GRPO. Intuitively, clipping discards gradient information. Can you reconcile this with PPO theory and explain why the token-level gradients in GRPO are so noisy that discarding more of them (via sequence-level clipping) can improve the signal-to-noise ratio and overall efficiency?

questions.title: Mechanism of MoE expert-activation volatility causing unstable token ratios
questions.question_body: You report that about $10\%$ of experts for the same sample change after each update in a 48-layer MoE model, which destabilizes token-level ratios $\frac{\pi_\theta(y_t\mid\cdot)}{\pi_{\theta_\text{old}}(y_t\mid\cdot)}$. Could you provide a concrete example or simplified model showing how a change in top-2 gating for one token can make $w_t$ spike, and why aggregating to a sequence-level ratio $s_i$ (geometric mean across tokens) is robust to such routing changes?

questions.title: Why is sequence likelihood more tolerant to precision differences between engines?
questions.question_body: The paper suggests GSPO can directly use sequence likelihoods from the inference engine (potentially with different precision) without recomputing in the training engine. Since $\pi_\theta(y\mid x)$ is a product of per-token probabilities, wouldn’t small per-token numerical discrepancies compound multiplicatively? Why is the sequence-level use in GSPO still robust, and is this mainly because the ratio is exponentiated by $1/|y|$ (geometric mean) and then tightly clipped?

questions.title: How do you handle near-zero reward variance within a group (division by zero in $\hat A$)?
questions.question_body: When rewards $\{r(x,y_i)\}_{i=1}^G$ are nearly identical, $\operatorname{std}(\{r\})$ can be very small. What is the practical strategy in GSPO for this case (e.g., add $\epsilon$ to the denominator, skip the batch, or fall back to a different baseline), and how sensitive is training to this choice?

questions.title: Where does KL regularization fit into GSPO and how does it interact with clipping?
questions.question_body: The paper omits the KL term for brevity. In practice, do you add a KL penalty to a reference policy or to $\pi_{\theta_\text{old}}$? How does a sequence-level KL penalty change the effective calibration of the sequence-level clipping range $\varepsilon$, and is there a recommended way to tune KL coefficients jointly with GSPO’s clipping?

questions.title: Is GSPO connected to reward-weighted regression or preference-based objectives like DPO/IPO?
questions.question_body: At a high level, GSPO scales gradients by a sequence-level weight and an advantage derived from rewards. Is there a formal connection to reward-weighted regression (e.g., maximizing $\mathbb{E}[r\,\log\pi_\theta]$) or to preference-based objectives such as DPO/IPO that also operate at the sequence level? Any equivalences or notable differences would help position GSPO among sequence-level training methods.

questions.title: Why not simply average or cap token-level ratios in GRPO to mimic GSPO?
questions.question_body: If GRPO’s instability comes from unequal token weights $w_{i,t}$, why not replace them with a per-sequence constant (e.g., the arithmetic or geometric mean of $\{w_{i,t}\}_t$) so that all tokens within a response share the same weight? Would that not recover GSPO’s key stability property, or is there a subtle difference due to how gradients and clipping are applied?
